state: video chroma, not ours. The clip is yuv420p tagged bt709; the refs were cut with ffmpeg's default .jpg path, which keeps the YCbCr and so gets decoded with BT.601. Same frame re-decoded as BT.709 (scale=in_color_matrix=bt709, .png): pit B/G 1.007/1.008 (jpg 0.960/0.957), frame 1.066/1.081 (jpg 1.009/1.022), menu 1.022/1.060, party 1.064/1.086. jpg minus 709 is 0 on neutrals and grows with saturation (G +0.8 at sat<15, +5..8 at sat>75; B -0.3 to -2.5), the signature of a matrix mismatch. Run 62 vs the 709 decode: pit B/G 1.038 (our sweep 1.009-1.053), frame 1.094 (+1-3%), menu 1.062 (+0-4%), party 1.104 (+2-4%); logo (neutral) 1.017 vs 1.023/1.007. Same check on A2 lounge pairs (same clip, same pipeline): ours/709 B/G 1.005-1.020. The remaining x1.09-1.17 in absolute B rides with G (pit G x1.11/x1.14): it is the pit luma above, not hue. All refs in docs/review/ref carry this bias (DECODING trap 39)

state: the logo's RGB fringe is the original shader's own timed glitch, shot at an open gate. Mtl_DE_UI_TITLE_Glitch has four flicker gates on _Time.y (frac(sin(floor(t*rate)*12.9898+seed)*43758.5) > 0.95: slice+chroma 10/s, jitter 9/s, warp 8/s, block 5/s), no animation or curve drives it; chroma offset 0.005 UV of the ripped 1024 atlas = the 1-2 px seen. Sweep A1c_LogoProbe.LogoOverTime (logo-run1, 182 shots, logo-sweep-run1.tsv): 7 shots with fringe (12-40% of bright logo pixels), all 7 with the slice gate predicted open; 0 fringe with it closed; 149/182 with all gates closed. Runs 60/61 hit an open gate (batchmode steps time by 1/3 s, so the shot time repeats). A1 now checks the gates at the render time and retakes at the next pose: run 62 t=85.742 all gates 0, |R-B|>90 on 0 of 7152 bright logo pixels (run 61: 2328 of 8534; 02.jpg: 0 of 7411; box 0.03-0.27 x 0.03-0.17, bright = max channel >180).
